title: THE SANCTIONS ARGUMENT
subtitle: Mapping the logical structure of the Western sanctions case against Russia.
source: IMF World Economic Outlook 2023; CREA Energy Institute; KSE Institute Russia sanctions tracker

data.text: Russia's GDP contracted 2.1% in 2022 despite record energy revenues.
Capital flight exceeded $250B in the first six months of the war.
data.attribution: CREA Energy Institute; Central Bank of Russia

claim.text: Western sanctions have imposed significant economic costs on Russia.

warrant.text: Economic contraction and capital flight indicate sanctions are creating measurable pressure on the target state.

backing.text: Historical precedent: Iran sanctions (2012), South Africa apartheid-era sanctions (1980s), Iraq sanctions regime (1990s).

qualifier.text: Though not sufficient to change Russia's war calculus in the near term.
qualifier.label: QUALIFIER

rebuttal.text: Russia fully reorients trade to non-sanctioning economies — which it is actively attempting via China, India, and the Gulf.
